title: MakeUseOf - Tech Writer
description:
This position will operate on a remote, contractual basis.
About MakeUseOf
MakeUseOf is one of the largest online technology publications on the web today. We equip millions of readers-from everyday consumers to seasoned tech enthusiasts-with practical guides, explainers, product recommendations, and deep feature analysis to help them make the most of their technology.
About the Role
MakeUseOf is looking for Freelance Features Writers across our core tech verticals. While we cover everything from desktop operating systems to smart home tech, we are actively looking for specialized writers who can turn complex technical subjects, hands-on builds, and practical home tech into clear, engaging features.
Priority Coverage Areas:

•
Home Automation & Practical DIY Tech: Smart home sensors (motion, occupancy, contact), smart hubs/protocols (Matter, Zigbee, Z-Wave), power tool ecosystems (Ryobi, Milwaukee, DeWalt), and AV/networking cabling infrastructure (Cat 6/6a, Ethernet drops, HDMI standards).

•
AI & Local Language Models: Writers with dedicated hardware rigs excited to test, benchmark, and write about open-source local LLMs (Ollama, LM Studio), local AI workflows, custom agents, and practical consumer AI applications.

•
Homelab & Advanced Networking: Deep knowledge of home networking infrastructure, Proxmox, NAS builds, self-hosting, network management tools, routers, radio networks, and home network security.

•
PC Hardware & Linux: Hands-on experience with CPUs, GPUs, benchmarking, custom PC building, hardware testing, and the Linux ecosystem.

•
Maker Projects & Hardware Hacking: Smart home automation, Raspberry Pi, ESP32 microcontrollers, DIY hardware builds, and practical workshop tech.

•
Core Operating Systems & Software: Windows, macOS, Android, iOS, security/privacy tools, productivity software, and web utilities.

Responsibilities:

• Proactively pitch creative, original feature ideas while regularly claiming assigned topics from the editorial board.

• Write clear, engaging, and structurally sound feature articles that simplify complex technical concepts.

• Test software, hardware, or workflows hands-on to provide authentic, step-by-step guidance and technical analysis.

• Input, format, and structure articles inside our in-house CMS according to style guidelines (including screenshots, formatting, and link insertion).

• Work collaboratively with section editors to refine pitches and incorporate feedback.

Application Requirements & Qualifications:

• Track record writing technical guides, hardware deep-dives, or software features in English.

• Access to the physical hardware, custom rigs, microcontrollers, homelab environments, or testing setups required for your primary coverage areas.

• Strong drive to consistently pitch fresh, relevant article ideas that match current tech trends.

• Ability to break down technical jargon into accessible, practical advice for tech enthusiasts and everyday readers alike.

How to Apply:
Please submit the following materials in your application:

• Your CV / Resume

• A Cover Letter addressing: Which specific topics/verticals above match your hands-on expertise, and what setups/gear (e.g., home networks, tool ecosystems, test rigs) do you currently use?

•
2-3 published writing samples (preferably long-form tech features, explainers, homelab guides, or hardware breakdowns).

We will get back to you as soon as possible if we think you'd make a solid addition to the team.

As a Business Analyst - MDM & Data Governance, you will serve as the bridge between business stakeholders and technical teams, helping define and deliver enterprise master data management and governance solutions. • 5+ years of Business Analyst experience, with demonstrated experience supporting Master Data Management (MDM), Data Governance, or Data Strategy initiatives.

• Strong understanding of Data Governance principles, including data stewardship, data ownership, metadata management, reference data, and data quality processes.

• Experience documenting match/merge rules, survivorship strategies, data definitions, governance workflows, and business process improvements.

• Experience working with SQL, reporting, and enterprise data platforms, with the ability to analyze data and support testing and validation activities.

The Koch Internship Program (KIP) is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the admissions process early!

Citizens Against Government Waste (CAGW) offers a wide variety of opportunities to college students across the country. Unpaid research, communications, and government affairs internships are available on a year-round basis and can vary in length from a semester to a few weeks in duration. Interns can choose to work part-time or full-time, as hours of work are extremely flexible. Our daily work with Capitol Hill and the White House, as well as government agencies and other nonprofit organizations, provides a close and invaluable look at how Washington works. Many projects involve working closely with staff members, while others require a great deal of independence. Interns are considered important members of our staff and actively participate in staff meetings and other events. While interns will also be required to perform clerical duties from time to time, much of the work will be substantive.
 
Research Internship
Assist in formulating policy papers and collect data for original investigative studies. - Du bringst deine tiefen WEG-Erfahrungen aus den Einsätzen zurück in unser Product-Team, um unsere Software stetig zu verbessern.

DU PASST GUT, WENN DU

title: Software Engineer, Networking
description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

HOW WE OPERATE

- Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

- Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

- Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

- Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

THE PRODUCTION ENGINEERING TEAM

Examples of key exciting problems the team is working on

- Turn every network fault from a mystery into a closed ticket: link diagnostics across router-router and NIC-to-router paths, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization that shows exactly what's broken and why. At this scale, debugging has to be systematic, not artisanal.

- Build the network repair pipeline that runs itself: from automated fault detection through RMA initiation, ticket integration, transceiver lifecycle tracking, and return to service, across DC fabric, edge, and host-to-network layers. When a new site comes online every six months, manual repair doesn't keep up.

- Build the network monitoring platform for a fleet that never stops growing: define requirements, alerting lifecycle, and health dashboards from scratch, for infrastructure spanning multiple hyperscale sites today and 10s to 100s of GWs ahead. It doesn't exist yet. We're building it.

 

ROLE SCOPE

- Own network fleet health end to end. Define the realtime monitoring requirements, build the alerting lifecycle, and ship the dashboards that give every on-call engineer a true picture of network state across all sites.

- Build active debugging tooling. Link diagnostics, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization - the tools that turn a network fault from a mystery into a solvable problem, fast.

- Turn repair into a pipeline, not a procedure. Build the automation that takes a network failure from detection through parts management and return to service. Ticket integration, repair lifecycle pipelines, transceiver and optics tracking - owned, not improvised.

- Own network qualification and validation. Build the frameworks that gate new sites and hardware into production. You define what a healthy network looks like before it carries traffic.

- Own end-to-end reliability, scalability, and operation of the network at-scale. Fluidstack is building one of the largest datacenter networks in the world and that can only be accomplished with aggressive automation, tooling, and incident discipline.

The FinOps Analyst will support financial management and cost optimization across Infrastructure and Technology. Infrastructure & Cloud Cost Management

• Monitor and analyze infrastructure and cloud hosting costs across environments and platforms.

• Help establish cost allocation, tagging, and ownership practices to improve infrastructure cost visibility.

Budget Planning & Forecasting

Mochi Medical, originally founded as an obesity management practice, is expanding its virtual care model beyond weight management. • Build rapport, credibility, and engagement with patients through exceptional communication.

• Use motivational interviewing to guide patients toward sustainable lifestyle change.

• Document visits in our EMR using our nutrition note templates.

• Stay current with research on obesity medicine, GLP-1 therapy and nutrition, binge eating disorder, and emerging specialty areas.

• Adapt to a fast-paced startup environment and contribute to team-wide improvements.

• Legally permitted to provide medical nutrition therapy in at least one state where Mochi sees patients. A state nutritionist license or certification is required for insurance-covered visits (see "A note on states" below) and is strongly preferred.

• Individual professional liability (malpractice) insurance, or willingness to obtain it before your start date.

• Proficient in online scheduling tools, EMR systems, and video-visit coordination.

• Skilled in motivational interviewing and patient education.

• Comfortable working in a dynamic, evolving startup environment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Current state license or certification as a nutritionist in one or more of: Florida, New York, Washington, North Carolina, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Minnesota, Massachusetts, Kentucky, Connecticut, New Mexico, Montana, Delaware, North Dakota, District of Columbia, or Alaska. • Experience with GLP-1 or other anti-obesity medications and the nutrition considerations that accompany them.

• Experience or interest in nutrition as it relates to dermatology, hormone replacement therapy, mental health, longevity, or hair loss.

• Bilingual (English/Spanish) (a plus).

title: Senior Paid Media Specialist
description:
Senior Paid Media Specialist - Reunion Marketing
Remote or hybrid (US) · Full time · Paid Media team · Automotive
Be the person the team calls
Reunion Marketing runs Google, Meta, and Microsoft ads for more than 200 automotive dealerships. When a campaign stops delivering, a feed gets disapproved, or a client's numbers do not add up, someone has to jump in, sort it out, and calm everyone down. We want that to be you.
This is a senior seat with real standing on the team. You will manage our biggest dealer groups, lead client conversations, and help every new specialist we hire get up to speed. No two days look the same, and you will rarely be working alone.
What your days look like

•
Many accounts, always moving. You run a portfolio of dealer accounts across Google Ads, Meta Ads, and Microsoft Advertising in the Fluency platform: budgets, bids, search terms, audiences, creative, and inventory updates, on a steady monthly rhythm.

•
Our most important clients. You own the largest dealer groups and the accounts with the most moving parts. You lead their monthly performance reviews and set the example the rest of the team follows.

•
The go-to when things break. Tracking, Tag Manager, GA4, inventory feeds, attribution, account setup: when a specialist gets stuck, they come to you. You find the cause, fix it, and write it down so nobody hits the same wall twice.

•
Teaching new teammates. You onboard and train every new Paid Media Specialist, from platform setup to client calls, and walk them through their first 90 days with regular check-ins.

•
Talking with people. Monthly calls with dealer principals and marketing directors, plus constant contact with Client Success and SEO. You explain what happened, what it means, and what we will do next, in plain language.

•
Keeping it organized. Accurate monthly reports, clean checklists, budgets paced to plan, and a knowledge base the whole team uses.

How success is measured
You will know exactly where you stand. We track cost per lead against each client's target, lead volume and return on ad spend, budget pacing, tracking and feed health, how quickly escalations get resolved, how fast your new hires ramp, and whether our biggest clients stay with us.
This role fits you if

• You like being in the middle of things: clients, teammates, and a dozen open tabs at once.

• You move quickly and like a day full of variety more than a day spent on one task.

• You have experience in the automotive industry.

• You are naturally organized and you notice the details others miss.

• You read people well, and you can turn a frustrated client into a calm one.

• You enjoy teaching and like seeing someone you trained succeed.

• You want your work to be seen, and you want a clear path to the next title.

What you bring

• 5+ years of hands-on Google Ads and Meta Ads experience, including advanced setup and troubleshooting

• Automotive digital marketing experience: inventory feeds, Google Merchant Center, and model-level campaigns

• Agency experience managing a multi-client portfolio, including large or high-touch accounts

• Working proficiency in GA4 and Google Tag Manager, including conversion tracking and attribution

• Experience in the Fluency platform

A plus: OEM co-op program experience, time spent training other paid media specialists, and Google Ads, GA4, Meta Blueprint, or Microsoft Advertising certifications.
Where this role leads
This seat is a step toward Paid Media Team Lead, Director of Digital Advertising, or a platform and automation lead role. Hold your top accounts, lift your new hires, and improve how the team works, and the next step is real.
What we offer

• Remote or hybrid work, your choice

• A senior seat with visible impact on our biggest clients and on the team

• A team that lives by Grit, Elevating Others, Embracing Discomfort, and Continuous Improvement

title: Investment Banking Compliance Analyst
description:
🚀 About Finalis

Finalis is the leading platform enabling independent and boutique investment banking firms to operate legally and compliantly. The firm provides regulatory affiliation and compliance infrastructure supporting private market transactions, including M&A, capital raising, private placements, secondary transactions, and alternative investments.

✨ About the role

The Investment Banking Compliance Analyst supports Finalis ’s investment banking and private markets business by providing compliance guidance throughout the transaction lifecycle. This role works directly with investment bankers and registered representatives on private placements, M&A engagements, and other private market transactions, from initial engagement and due diligence through closing.

We are looking for someone who is intellectually curious and enjoys understanding how transactions work. The strongest candidate will be comfortable analyzing complex or unfamiliar structures, asking thoughtful questions, and becoming a trusted compliance resource to our bankers.

✍️ What you'll do

Transaction & Regulatory Review

• Review proposed investment banking engagements, engagement letters, compensation arrangements, and transaction structures for compliance with applicable securities laws, FINRA requirements, and Finalis policies.

• Review private securities offerings and applicable Securities Act exemptions, with particular emphasis on Regulation D and Rules 506(b) and 506(c).

• Analyze M&A, secondary, and other private market transactions for applicable securities-law and broker-dealer considerations.

• Review M&A transactions under the federal M&A broker exemption framework and identify circumstances requiring registered broker-dealer involvement.

• Support applicable FINRA private placement requirements, including Rules 5122 and 5123.

Due Diligence & Transaction Execution

• Conduct risk-based due diligence on issuers, sponsors, control persons, and other relevant transaction parties and evaluate identified red flags.

• Review offering materials, organizational documents, financial information, transaction agreements, and other relevant diligence materials.

• Work with bankers to resolve diligence and compliance questions and appropriately document conclusions, conditions, and approvals.

• Monitor transactions for material changes and review transaction and closing documentation for consistency with the approved structure.

• Support transactions through closing, including satisfaction of applicable compliance conditions, books and records, and required regulatory filings.

Banker & Business Partnership

• Serve as a day-to-day compliance resource for investment bankers and registered representatives.

• Participate in transaction calls and work directly with bankers to understand proposed structures and resolve regulatory and compliance questions.

• Ask thoughtful questions to understand the economic substance of transactions rather than relying solely on labels or form.

• Translate regulatory requirements into clear, practical guidance while maintaining sound compliance judgment.

• Stay current on regulatory developments affecting private placements, M&A, and private market transactions.

🔎 Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.

• 3+ years of relevant experience in broker-dealer compliance, investment banking, securities law, private markets, or a related field.

• Working knowledge of private placements and exemptions from Securities Act registration, particularly Regulation D.

• Familiarity with FINRA requirements applicable to private placements and investment banking activities.

• Ability to understand complex transaction structures and legal, financial, and offering documents.

• Strong analytical skills, sound judgment, and intellectual curiosity.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills and comfort working directly with investment bankers and other sophisticated stakeholders.

title: Senior Reconciliation Specialist
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life - or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

As a Senior Reconciliation Specialist, you’ll be a subject-matter expert in safeguarding and reconciliations for Vinted Pay. You’ll own the daily control that protects “Relevant Funds” (client money) and keeps client and company funds strictly segregated, take on the most complex investigations, and drive the projects and documentation that keep our safeguarding framework scalable and audit-ready. You’ll work closely with the Team Manager, Finance, Treasury, Compliance, Payments and Tech, and with our banking and PSP partners

In this position, you’ll 

• Own the daily internal and external safeguarding reconciliations and the end-of-day safeguarding control across all accounts, currencies and banking partners, making sure any shortfall or excess is corrected within regulatory timelines.

• Perform monthly PSP invoice, fee and settlement reconciliations and resolve discrepancies with partners.

• Investigate complex cash management, FX and safeguarding issues (e.g. funding shortfalls, FX differences, unallocated funds, cut-off mismatches), quantify the impact and work with Payments, Operations and Tech to fix root causes.

• Support the Team Manager on escalated issues, such as high-value or aged breaks, partner disputes and potential safeguarding incidents.

• Act as the reconciliation and safeguarding expert on third-party platform implementations (reconciliation tools, banking partners, PSPs, new currencies): define requirements, run UAT and support go-live.

• Identify manual bottlenecks and deliver automation with Data and Tech.

• Write and maintain process descriptions, procedures, control documentation and the Safeguarding Policy, and keep an audit-ready break and incident log.

• Prepare daily and monthly safeguarding regulatory reporting and support internal and external audits.

• Share expertise with colleagues and track regulatory developments (e.g. PSD2/PSD3, EMD, FCA CASS 15).

About you 

• 4+ years in reconciliations, safeguarding, treasury operations or finance controls in an EMI, payment institution, bank or high-volume fintech.

• Hands-on experience with safeguarding or client-money reconciliations, controls and audits, and a strong grasp of segregation of funds, general ledger accounting and payment flows (PSP settlements, payouts, FX).

• Experience implementing or configuring a reconciliation platform (e.g. AutoRek, Ledge, Aurum, Duco) or contributing to finance-system projects.

• Working SQL and advanced Excel; experience with BI or planning

Paying vendors is one of the most manual, error-prone jobs in finance. Invoices arrive by email and PDF, get keyed in by hand, wait on approvals, and then have to be paid on time, by the right method, for the right amount, and recorded correctly in the books. A single mistake can mean a late fee, a duplicate payment, or an unhappy vendor.

Ramp's Bill Pay team builds the accounts payable system that automates that work end to end: bill intake and parsing, approvals, payment execution by ACH, check, card, and international transfer, vendor credits, and sync to customers' accounting systems. Bill Pay is one of Ramp's fastest-growing products, and businesses rely on it every day to move large amounts of money.

We're looking for a senior backend engineer to own a core part of that system. You'll take responsibility for an area such as payment execution, bill intake and AI-powered extraction, approvals, or accounting sync, set its technical direction within the team, and keep it correct and reliable as volume grows. You'll work closely with product, design, and payments partners to make accounts payable faster and more trustworthy for finance teams.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the design and evolution of a core Bill Pay system, such as payment execution, bill intake, approvals, or accounting sync, from technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration

- Build payment workflows that move money correctly across ACH, check, card, and international rails, with strong safeguards against duplicate, late, or incorrect payments

- Build AI-powered AP automation, including invoice extraction, auto-coding, and agents that reduce manual review for finance teams

- Design data models that keep every bill, approval, payment, and credit accurate and traceable through to the general ledger

- Build reliable integrations with ERPs and accounting systems that stay consistent through retries, partial failures, and edits on either side

- Improve the reliability, performance, and observability of Bill Pay systems as customers process larger payment volumes

- Drive technical direction for your area and raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

- Experience designing, building, and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows

- A track record of owning a system or product area end to end and shaping its technical direction over time

- Strong system design judgment, especially around correctness, idempotency, and reliability in systems where mistakes have real financial impact

- Product sense: you care about the customer problem, not just the ticket, and you balance speed with quality

- Clear communication and a collaborative approach to technical decisions across product, design, and engineering

NICE TO HAVES

- Experience with accounts payable, payments, money movement, or other financial systems

- Experience building integrations with ERPs or accounting systems, such as NetSuite or QuickBooks

About Us

Rho is on a mission to make finance frictionless for organizations. Our team and technology power high-performing companies with an all-in-one, end-to-end finance platform that lets organizations safely manage cash and spending across commercial-grade banking, corporate cards, treasury management, expense management, accounts payable, and more.

Our customers run their banking, cards, and payments through Rho. We are splitting a large Python monolith into Go and Python services on GCP, and shipping a public API, agents, and MCP surfaces. Security is part of the product.

The Team

Security at Rho is small: a VCISO, one security engineer in Poland, and the engineers who ship. You will be the first US security engineer. We plan to grow this into a team over the next six months, and you will help pick who.

The Role

Hands-on. You write production code most days. You own product and platform security, and you own finding queues and incident response until we hire for detection and response.

What you'll do
Product Security

- Threat model new systems and review designs with the teams that own them before they ship.

- Build the paved road: secure defaults, guardrails in CI, dependency and supply chain checks, so the safe way is the easy way.

- Own the vulnerability lifecycle: triage findings from Pensar, Semgrep, CodeQL, Dependabot, pentests, and inbound researcher reports; hold the SLAs; write the fix or get it written; track remediation to zero. Stand up our vulnerability disclosure program.

Platform Security

- Harden GCP and GKE: least-privilege IAM, workload identity, secrets, network policy, environment separation, all in Terraform.

- Secure our LLM, agent, and MCP surfaces: guardrails, sandboxes, agents as identities with scoped access, prompt injection detection.

Detection & Response

- Own detections in our SIEM, tune signal to noise, keep the runbooks current, stand up on the call rotation, and lead incidents end to end: triage, contain, investigate, remediate, post-mortem.

- Run tabletop exercises and hunt for what detections miss.

What we're looking for

- 6+ years in security engineering, or software engineering with a security focus. You ship code and tools, not only findings.

- Depth in one of product security, cloud and platform security, or detection and response, and working knowledge of the other two.

- Comfortable changing production and owning the outcome. Python or Go, Kubernetes, Terraform, one major cloud.

- You can triage competing risks and trade security against velocity without slowing the team down.

- Clear writer: design reviews, runbooks and incident reports engineers actually read.

NICE TO HAVE

- Fintech, payments or another regulated industry. PCI DSS or SOC 2 evidence work.

- Bug bounty, red team, CVEs, talks, or open source.

- Hands-on AI security: guardrails, agent identities, prompt injection.

Axon is scaling its global manufacturing operations, and the finance team behind that growth needs sharp, detail-oriented analysts to keep it running with precision. As a Cost Accountant on our Cost Accounting team, you'll sit at the intersection of finance and operations, owning month-end close activities, driving inventory and variance analysis, and partnering directly with FP&A, Supply Chain Controllership, and Operations leaders. This is a newly created, high-visibility role where your work directly shapes how Axon understands and manages the cost of bringing life-saving technology to market.

title: English Language Expert (Great Britain)
description:
Role Title: English Language Expert (Great Britain)
Role Type: Contractor
Location: Great Britain, Remote
micro1 is engaging English Language Experts (Great Britain) to contribute to a customer's innovative audio annotation initiative focused on British English. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. This opportunity emphasizes the importance of written and verbal communication, aiming for those with a passion for language and a keen ear for the diversity of British dialects and accents. Whether you have experience in teaching, transcription, editing, translation, or journalism, your insights into the nuances of British English will directly influence linguistic technology advancements.
Scope of Work

• Listen to multi-speaker conversational audio recordings, identifying and tagging key speaker and audio metadata such as dialect, accent, audio quality, background noise, age, and speaking style.

• Annotate and correct first-pass ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) transcripts, ensuring precise application of British English spelling, usage, and conventions.

• Utilize your knowledge of British regional accents-from Received Pronunciation and Estuary English to Scouse, Geordie, Yorkshire, Mancunian, West Country, Welsh English, and Scottish English-to accurately identify and categorize dialectal features.

• Apply your knowledge of British vocabulary, idioms, slang, and spelling to enhance the linguistic accuracy of project data.

• Maintain detailed and consistent annotation standards throughout all assigned project tasks.

Preferred Qualifications

• Fluent proficiency in British English, with demonstrated familiarity across multiple dialects and regional accents.

• Background in language teaching, linguistics, transcription, editing, translation, journalism, or a related discipline.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a meticulous approach to language variation and usage.

• Ability to distinguish subtle differences in British English pronunciation and vocabulary.

• Experience working with audio data, metadata tagging, or transcription practices is beneficial.

• Adaptable, detail-oriented, and able to manage complex annotation guidelines independently.

• Interest in linguistic technology, AI training, or language data projects is a plus.
